correctness.rationale: The kernel is reconstructed from an orthonormal affine basis for all strictly positive Bernoulli marginals. Conditioned two-point row kernels give a piecewise-affine monotonicity lemma, proving rare-vertex sharpness and endpoint equality via kernel symmetry. Explicit positive-probability binomial events give strict global fair minimization. Negative-part bounds give a strict upper bound 2n-1 and exact limiting sharpness; an n=4 support decomposition proves all three exact rational values, which put the homogeneous norm strictly between two unequal-parameter norms of the same mean. Independent exact Gram-matrix checks passed 4863 finite assertions, supplementary to universal proof.

value.rationale: The natural heterogeneous first-degree Bernoulli least-squares stability problem is solved for all dimensions and arbitrary marginals, locating the sharp row, giving componentwise monotonic control and the unique globally best marginal design. Two explicit 4-coordinate equal-mean counterexamples show that mean-preserving heterogeneity can either raise or lower the sharp norm: the stability functional is neither Schur-convex nor Schur-concave on that bias slice. The homogeneous norm cannot be safely extrapolated to heterogeneous populations from the average bias. This constitutes a complete classification and nontrivial parameter-ordering result, not merely code or an unmotivated finite example.
